title: Pointwise representability assembles into a coherent infinity adjunction
statement: Use infinity categories, mapping spaces and coherent functors as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in fixed universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and with small mapping spaces, where small means $\mathcal U$-small and the categories fit in $\mathcal U'$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor; no presentability or completeness is assumed. It has a right adjoint if and only if for each $d\in\mathcal D$ the presheaf $c\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(c),d)$ is representable, that is, naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,r_d)$ for some $r_d\in\mathcal C$. Dually a functor $i:\mathcal E\to\mathcal C$ has a left adjoint if and only if for each $c\in\mathcal C$ the covariant functor $e\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$ is representable by an object of $\mathcal E$. The representing objects assemble to a coherent functor and an equivalence of mapping-space bifunctors; the universal representing maps are its unit or counit. The resulting adjunction has coherent units, counits and triangle identities, including their higher compatibility data.

proof.text: Suppose $F\dashv R$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$ as in [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence] with $G=R$. For every $c,d$ it gives the mapping-space equivalence $a\mapsto R(a)\eta_c$, with inverse homotopy class represented by $\Psi_c(b)=\epsilon_dF(b)$. Thus every $\Psi_c$ is an equivalence of full spaces. To make these components one coherent transformation, apply the inverse clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] to $\mathcal E=\mathcal C$, $a=Rd$, the presheaf $P_d(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$ (whose action on $t$ is precomposition with $F(t)$) and the point $\epsilon_d\in P_d(Rd)$: it gives a coherent transformation $h_{Rd}\to P_d$ whose component at $c$ is $b\mapsto P_d(b)(\epsilon_d)=\epsilon_d\circ F(b)=\Psi_c(b)$. Every vertex component is an equivalence, so by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. Setting $r_d=Rd$ proves representability of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(F(-),d)$.

source.place: Necessity paragraph, expanded unit/counit computation; Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1); coherence via Definition 5.6.6.1 (038A) and Theorem 4.4.4.4 (01DK), componentwise detection of natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: Suppose $L\dashv i$ with unit $\eta'$ and counit $\epsilon'$ as in [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence] with $F=L$, $G=i$, $x=c$ and $d=e$. It gives the equivalence $\Phi'_e:a\mapsto i(a)\eta'_c$ on the entire mapping space, with inverse represented by $b\mapsto\epsilon'_eL(b)$. The covariant clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], applied to $Q_c(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$ and $\eta'_c\in Q_c(Lc)$, gives a coherent transformation $h^{Lc}\to Q_c$ with components $a\mapsto i(a)\circ\eta'_c=\Phi'_e(a)$; by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)$, so $Lc$ represents $Q_c$.

proof.text:
Assume the right-adjoint representability condition and fix $d$. Choose an equivalence of coherent presheaves $\theta_d:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,r_d)\simeq P_d$, where $P_d(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d)$. The Yoneda evaluation statement [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] applies because the mapping spaces are small and $\theta_d$ is coherent, not merely a collection of objectwise equivalences. Put $\epsilon_d=\theta_d(r_d)(\operatorname{id}_{r_d}):F(r_d)\to d$. The inverse formula in that statement identifies $\theta_d(c)$, on the entire mapping space and with its coherent naturality, with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,r_d)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fc,d),\qquad t\longmapsto\epsilon_d\circ F(t).$$
Consequently these actual composition maps are equivalences for every $c$. No choice of maps $r_d\to r_{d'}$ has been assumed.

source.place: Sufficiency: conversion of a representing equivalence to the universal arrow, by Kerodon 03M5 and its opposite.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal], the comparison maps of step 3 become, on opposite mapping spaces, $v\mapsto F^{\mathrm{op}}(v)\circ\epsilon_d^{\mathrm{op}}$. Naturality in $F$ and compatibility with composition identify these maps, up to the specified homotopies, with the original maps under the reversal equivalences. They are therefore equivalences for every $c$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] to $F^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $x_d=r_d$ and $u_d=\epsilon_d^{\mathrm{op}}$. It gives a coherent $L\dashv F^{\mathrm{op}}$, without functorial initial choices or completeness assumptions. These outputs are coherent adjunction data in the sense of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. The functor simplicial sets are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; a $2$-simplex on $\eta F^{\mathrm{op}},F^{\mathrm{op}}\epsilon$ has long edge homotopic to the identity, and filling an inner horn $\Lambda^3_2$ against that homotopy gives the triangle with degenerate long edge; likewise for $L\eta,\epsilon L$. By [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] for the cospan $\{d\}\to\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\leftarrow\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, the mapping space of $(d\downarrow F^{\mathrm{op}})$ from $(Ld,\eta_d)$ to $(z,w)$ is the homotopy fiber over $w$ of the equivalence $v\mapsto F^{\mathrm{op}}(v)\eta_d$, hence contractible: $(Ld,\eta_d)$ is initial. Dually the inverse $u\mapsto\epsilon_zL(u)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence] makes $(F^{\mathrm{op}}z,\epsilon_z)$ terminal in $(L\downarrow z)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1 (02FV), applied to the opposite functor; mapping reversal is the existing op-mapping-reversal node and coherent-adjunction reversal is the new opposite-adjunction-data node.

proof.text: With $L\dashv F^{\mathrm{op}}$ the coherent adjunction data of step 4, [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-adjunction-data] supplies $F\dashv R$ for $R=L^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the reversed coherent unit, counit, universal arrows and triangles. Its counit components are universal representing maps, so take $r_d=R(d)$, replacing the initial representatives by equivalent ones. Finally [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence] applied to this adjunction gives the equivalence of mapping-space bifunctors, with its coherent parameter dependence.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1 (02FV) applied to the opposite functor, then order reversal of the adjunction (Kerodon 02EK with 003L); expanded by the agent.

proof.text: For dual sufficiency fix $c$ and choose a coherent equivalence $\lambda_c:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(l_c,-)\simeq Q_c$, where $Q_c(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,i(e))$. The covariant clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] sends it to $u_c=\lambda_c(l_c)(\operatorname{id}_{l_c}):c\to i(l_c)$ and identifies its component at $e$ with $v\mapsto i(v)\circ u_c$. This is therefore an equivalence for every $e$, including all parameters. Now use [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] with $R=i$, $\mathcal X=\mathcal E$, $\mathcal Y=\mathcal C$, $x_c=l_c$ and this $u_c$. It supplies a coherent $L\dashv i$, natural equivalences of the two-variable mapping-space functors, and coherent unit, counit and triangle homotopies. Exactly as in step 4, inner-horn filling in the functor quasicategories of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] gives the triangle $2$-simplices, and [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] with the equivalences $v\mapsto i(v)\eta_c$, respectively their inverses $u\mapsto\epsilon_eL(u)$ from [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence], makes $(Lc,\eta_c)$ initial in $(c\downarrow i)$ and $(i(e),\epsilon_e)$ terminal in $(L\downarrow e)$; so these are data of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. The unit components are universal representing maps, so take $l_c=L(c)$. In both variances this is an adjunction in the coherent infinity-categorical sense delivered by the criterion: its transformations and homotopies retain their higher compatibility as coherent diagrams, rather than only as equations in the ordinary homotopy category. Together with steps 1 and 2 this proves both equivalences in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem infinity_pointwise_adjoint_criterion (C D E : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory C] [Quasicategory D] [Quasicategory E] (_hC : HasSmallMappingSpaces.{u, v} C) (_hD : HasSmallMappingSpaces.{u, v} D) (_hE : HasSmallMappingSpaces.{u, v} E) (F : C ⟶ D) (i : E ⟶ C) : ((∃ R : D ⟶ C, Nonempty (HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelInfinity.CoherentAdjunction F R)) ↔ ∀ d : D _⦋0⦌, ∃ r : C _⦋0⦌, MappingPresheafRepresentedBy F d r true) ∧ ((∀ d : D _⦋0⦌, ∃ r : C _⦋0⦌, MappingPresheafRepresentedBy F d r true) → ∃ R : D ⟶ C, Nonempty (HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelInfinity.CoherentAdjunction F R) ∧ MappingBifunctorsEquivalent F R) ∧ ((∃ L : C ⟶ E, Nonempty (HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelInfinity.CoherentAdjunction L i)) ↔ ∀ c : C _⦋0⦌, ∃ l : E _⦋0⦌, MappingPresheafRepresentedBy i c l false) ∧ ((∀ c : C _⦋0⦌, ∃ l : E _⦋0⦌, MappingPresheafRepresentedBy i c l false) → ∃ L : C ⟶ E, Nonempty (HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelInfinity.CoherentAdjunction L i) ∧ MappingBifunctorsEquivalent L i)
lean.note: Both variances. Each criterion is stated as an iff between existence of a coherent adjoint (CoherentAdjunction alone, so necessity needs nothing more) and pointwise representability, plus the sufficiency clause that the representing objects assemble to an adjoint with a natural equivalence of mapping-space bifunctors. Representability and the bifunctor equivalence are in their equivalent right/left-fibration and correspondence models. Small mapping spaces are small Kan models, not degreewise smallness. The two universe levels explicitly render the size convention in the statement. Published coherent-adjunction data are reused, with their definition extracted to an existing binding to avoid a dependency on the downstream Quillen theorem.
